summary: Avi Loeb's appointment to lead a UAP risk investigation council drew attention this week alongside ongoing questions about government transparency and whistleblower protections. Luis Elizondo continued to feature prominently in discussions about past secrecy efforts, with journalist Ross Coulthart pushing back against what he calls "infighting" within the UAP community. Meanwhile, declassification efforts gained momentum, particularly around the 1952 Washington D.C. UFO encounter, with lawmakers pressing for release of related materials. AARO released several technical documents examining potential misidentifications (including Starlink satellite flaring and optical perspective effects), while the FY2026 NDAA UAP briefing deadline passed at the end of June. The week also included reporting on a missing scientist with a quantum physics background and continued discussion of UAP incursions near military bases, suggesting the conversation is expanding beyond historical cases into current operational concerns.
